# Requirements Document: Adding ancillaries to an order

## Introduction

A flight-related ancillary enters an order only with a flight for the same
passenger and segment, in the same request or already in the order.  The
sources never define flight related.  The taxonomy gives one answer: services
under Flight are flight related and services under Journey, such as insurance,
are not.  The model takes the answer as a parameter, a reading of the sources.

These requirements are generated from the Lean model in [`Rules/OneOrder/Ancillaries/Add.lean`](https://github.com/samdengler/airline-order-verified/blob/main/Rules/OneOrder/Ancillaries/Add.lean). Each acceptance criterion carries the status the build computed for it: *proven* means a theorem the build checked, *example only* means a computed example, *open* means a theorem the build could not prove, and *not checked* means no theorem or example covers it yet.

## Requirements

### Requirement ONE-602

**User Story:** As an airline, I want a bag or a seat sold only with the flight it is for, so that no customer pays for an ancillary on a flight they do not hold.

**Rule:** WHEN a seller adds services to an order THE SYSTEM SHALL accept the request only if every flight-related ancillary in it has a live flight service for its passenger and segment, in the order or in the request. (Lean: `addServices`)

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. IF a seller adds a flight-related ancillary for a passenger on a segment, and neither the order nor the request holds a live flight service for that passenger on that segment THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL refuse the request.
   - ONE-602.1, proven: proven theorem `add_refuses_without_flight`; example `addingAncillaries`
2. WHEN a request to add services is accepted THE SYSTEM SHALL add its order items after the existing ones and leave the existing ones as they were.
   - ONE-602.2, proven: proven theorem `add_appends`; example `addingAncillaries`
3. WHERE no service in a request is a flight-related ancillary THE SYSTEM SHALL accept the request.
   - ONE-602.3, proven: proven theorem `add_accepts_unrelated`; example `addingAncillaries`
4. WHEN a seller changes an order item of an order in which every live flight-related ancillary has a live flight service for its passenger and segment THE SYSTEM SHALL keep a live flight service for the passenger and segment of every live flight-related ancillary.
   - ONE-602.4, open: open theorem `change_keeps_flights`; counterexample `bagLeftByFlightChange`

#### Open question on ONE-602.4

> When every live flight-related ancillary of an order has a live flight
> service for its passenger and segment, a paid change to an order item keeps it
> so.
>
> Open question for the business.  The guide states the rule when an ancillary
> is bought.  A change that moves a passenger's flight to another segment
> cancels the old flight service and leaves the bag bought for it confirmed, on
> a segment the passenger no longer flies.  The example
> `bagLeftByFlightChange` shows it.  Does the rule hold for the life of the
> order, and if so, what happens to the bag?
